finding: On this hybrid (DeltaNet + GQA) model the state is NOT a per-token speed lever. Total state traffic 316 MB/token = ~0.67 ms = ~2.3% of the ~29 ms token. GQA KV (the thing KV-precision-reduction usually targets) is only 2.49 MB/token and grows sub-linearly with context (still << the 13.6 GB weights even at 32k). The dominant state traffic is the DeltaNet recurrent state (302 MB rw/token, 151 MB resident, CONTEXT-INDEPENDENT) whose precision is bound to recurrence stability (Doctor risk).
G8_verdict: MEASURED NEGATIVE as a speed lever: KV precision reduction on GQA saves ~0 (2.49 MB/token). rec_state precision (fp32->fp16) could save ~0.32 ms (~1% token) but risks recurrence stability. Not worth disturbing for speed (S012 section 11).
G9_verdict: The state is already small and mostly fixed-size; latent-KV/compression has little per-token headroom here. The hybrid's fixed DeltaNet state is a RESIDENCY advantage (flat long-context slope, confirmed), not a cost problem. Record as science; do not spend GPU on it while the MLP/representation front is open.
reopen_if: state exceeds ~5% of the token at a target context (e.g. GQA KV at very long context), or a successor architecture with growing state is adopted.
